packs.title: Galleries, gardens and public park views
packs.promise: Compare actual displays, make original pages and explore bounded visitor paths.

q.s: Collect how three works direct attention.
st: Choose three available works in one opened gallery. Identify one visible choice in each: a material, repeated form, boundary or arrangement. No particular work or temporary exhibition is required.

For each choice, describe what you actually see, then paraphrase one related point in the public interpretation when available. Keep an observation separate from a supplied statement or your own inference.
Compare two records. Write how their choices guide attention differently, without assigning an artist a motive that the display does not establish.
Finish three records and a comparison. Write after leaving the gallery if needed; no copied artwork, panel or complete exhibition view is required.

q.s: Design two small garden zones from observed forms.
st: From opened display-garden paths, choose three actual forms: for example a leaf outline, an upright stem pattern and a ground-level grouping. Record only what is present.
Make an original two-zone planting plan in notes or on paper. Give each zone a purpose you invent, such as a place to pause or a view from a window; do not present it as a real garden proposal.
Use your three observed forms in the plan and explain where each appears. Change their arrangement rather than copying a complete display or planting design.
Finish the two zones and three observation-to-design links. Drawing skill, plant identification and buying plants are not required.

q.s: Compare the outward and returning view on one public trail.
st: At the opened trailhead, record one fixed built detail you can use to recognize your return point. Remain on the paved public trail.
Travel outward for up to five minutes, turning sooner at the first bridge, road crossing, work barrier or crowded pinch point. No minimum distance or crossing is required.
At the turn, record one change in your view or surroundings. Return by the same opened path and compare the view facing the other way.
Finish the start detail, turn-point observation and one outward-versus-return difference. Stop and write from a clear place, not while moving.

packs.title: Downtown and Cobbham public paths
packs.promise: Read actual public buildings, compare gallery materials and make original pages across two afternoons.

q.t: Three ways to read a house
q.s: Collect three kinds of evidence inside a house museum.
st: Enter the actually opened house-museum visitor area. Find three available ways the house’s history is communicated: a room feature, an interpreted object or a public display can qualify.
For each, record one visible feature and paraphrase one related point actually supplied by the museum. Mark an unanswered question when the interpretation is insufficient.
Compare two records. Write one difference between what you can see directly and what you learn from the interpretation.
Finish three evidence records and the comparison after exit if necessary. Do not copy a room installation, full panel or an object’s decorative design.

q.s: Collect how materials meet in actual displayed work.
st: Enter an actually opened contemporary exhibition gallery. Choose three visible places where materials or forms meet in the displayed work.
For each meeting, describe what is visible without touching it. Paraphrase one relevant public interpretation point when available; mark a question when uncertain.
Compare two records. Write how their differences affect what you notice, without assigning an artist a motive unsupported by the display.
Finish three material-meeting records and a comparison after exit if necessary. Do not copy a complete work, portrait or exhibition installation.

q.t: Two pages for a made-up show
q.s: Translate exterior forms into two original page layouts.
st: Observe two actual exterior forms from a lawful public viewpoint, such as an opening rhythm and a roof or facade edge. Keep a busy entry clear.
Make two original page layouts for an unnamed fictional show, using boxes or written layout descriptions. Use the same two observed forms differently in each.
Mark where a fictional title and time could go, without adding a real venue, artist or event claim. Explain one difference between your two arrangements.
Finish both layouts and the observation links. No drawing skill, public performance or posting of the designs is required.
